SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

4. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

7. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

10. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.

12. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.

15. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

16. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
